protocol: On one fresh local graph per trial, seed control-plane facts, register the requested read-head count, warm cache entries, then submit one tokenized transaction retracting Enabled=false and asserting Enabled=true. If acknowledged, require the first pointed read at snapshotSeq 2 and 500 subsequent complete warm reads at snapshotSeq 2 with cacheHits=1 and validations balanced across heads.

results.stopReason: The canonical baseline correctly wrote/read the new snapshot; the read-head-only harness subsequently stopped because this path did not satisfy its cache-hit assertion.

results.outcome: Graph write failed; delivery may be unknown.
Both writes failed with delivery unknown; retained local ledger state remained nonterminal/atomic-delegated. Recovery was not inspected for these runs.

All seven attempts stopped at publication without confirmed completion; instrumented attempts returned delivery-unknown errors. At initial inspection retained local ledger state was nonterminal/atomic-delegated.

recoveryInspection.method: Reopened retained local state without issuing another application write; queried transaction status and pointed value, waited 12 seconds with the Durable Object alarm runtime active, then queried again.

interpretation: The one-trial success at 1 head and two at 8 heads do not estimate near-100% reliability. The 8-head repeat completed 500 pointed and 500 compound reads before the write at concurrency 16/128, then 500/500 warm reads after a committed flip. At 12/16/100 heads, the immediate public write result was unknown; one retained 100-head transaction was later observed completing through the durable alarm while a complete pointed query returned the new snapshot before and after recovery. This demonstrates one eventual local recovery, not immediate acknowledgement or a recovery-latency bound. These outcomes do not establish a provider limit or stable numerical head threshold. Cold/unique strict-latest read scaling, hosted performance, open-loop load and recovery under injected faults remain untested.
limitations: All experiments used local Miniflare/SQLite and historical source a38765e; the active implementation was not changed.

One transaction per fresh graph; no repeated statistical sample at successful head counts, mixed writes, injected recovery faults, sustained availability, multi-region placement or Cloudflare limits tested. Only one 100-head pending transaction was observed through alarm recovery for 12 seconds.
No full formal model check was rerun for this publication probe.
The diagnostic harness did not issue an application write replay; the observed completion was performed by the Durable Object transaction ledger's scheduled alarm.
